text: A fool squanders away, without credit or advantage to himself, more than a man of sense spends with both. The latter employs his money as he does his time, and never spends a shilling of the one, nor a minute of the other, but in something that is either useful or rationally pleasing to himself or others.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter LXII, to his son, London, January 10, Old Style 1749
